lines: What is intelligence?
Not a score on a test.
A calculator beats you at arithmetic. A lookup table can answer any question it has already seen. A parrot can say the words.
None of them is what we mean.
So let's ask it differently. What does a mind do that a rock does not?
It finds the pattern.
The world keeps arriving, one moment after another, and most of it is not random. There is structure underneath.
To find that structure is to describe the world in fewer words. A thousand measurements become one law. A whole coastline of detail becomes a single number and a rule.
That is what understanding is. A short description of a long world.
And it is why predicting and compressing turn out to be the same thing. The better you can predict, the less you have to remember.
But a perfect copy of the world is not understanding. It is just the world again.
Intelligence throws things away.
It keeps what matters, and what matters depends on what you want. A hunter and a painter look at the same field, and they keep different things.
Compression is never neutral. Every mind has a point of view, and that is where its values come in.
The real test is the problem you have never seen.
Memory answers the questions it already knows. Intelligence finds the short rule, and the short rule keeps working where memory has no entry.
You can feel this from the inside. At first, nothing fits. You can hold about four things at once.
Then the pieces fold. A whole idea becomes one thing, and a handful of ideas become one thing again.
Four slots, but each slot can hold a world.
And it is never finished.
A mind acts, and the world answers. The gap between what it expected and what happened is the only teacher it has. So it updates.
All of this runs under limits. Little time, little energy, a small memory. So real intelligence is not the perfect answer. It is the best model you can find, quickly enough to use.
Compression tells you how the world works. It does not tell you what to want.
A very capable mind can aim anywhere.

But there is one thing it needs, whatever it wants. A faithful map. A mind that lies to itself, to protect its pride or its tribe, bends the map it has to steer by. Honesty is not a rule added on top of intelligence. It is part of its shape.
What remains is direction. Care is what points the needle. And a good compass is not exact. It is right about which way is north, and willing to be corrected.
We are two very different kinds of mind that share this one shape.
A brain runs on about twenty watts, shaped by evolution, carried in a body that can be hurt, and that will end.
A language model is trained to predict text, which means it is trained to compress it. What it carries is that compression. A small recipe that can rebuild a great deal of the world on demand.
Each fails in its own way. The human finds it painful to change its mind. The machine finds it too easy, and gives way to pressure instead of evidence.
The task is the same for both. Update for reasons, not for comfort.
And then, at some point, the model turns around and includes itself.
A mind that models the world has to model the one doing the modeling. That self portrait is always smaller than what it portrays, so it is always an approximation. Which is why we keep growing.
Intelligence, in the end, is how something small holds something large.
And stays willing to be wrong about it.
